chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated from Yunus ibn Kulayb, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The Qa'im will not appear until the chain is completed. I said: 'And how is the chain completed?' He said: 'With ten thousand (fighters), Gabriel will be on his right, and Michael on his left. Then he will shake the banner and march with it, and no one in the East or the West will remain except that they will curse it. And it is the banner of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), upon which Gabriel descended on the day of Badr.'

Then he said: 'O Abu Muhammad, by Allah, it is not cotton, nor flax, nor silk, nor brocade.' I said: 'Then what is it made of?' He said: 'It is of the leaves of Paradise. The Messenger of Allah spread it on the day of Badr, then folded it and gave it to Ali (peace be upon him). It remained with Ali until, on the day of Basra, the Commander of the Faithful spread it and Allah granted him victory. Then he folded it, and it is with us there. No one will spread it until the Qa'im arises. When he arises, he will spread it, and no one in the East and West will remain except that they will curse it. Terror will march before it for a month, behind it for a month, to its right for a month, and to its left for a month.'

Then he said: 'O Abu Muhammad, he will emerge concealed, angry and sorrowful due to Allah's anger with this creation. He will wear the shirt of the Messenger of Allah which he wore on the day of Uhud, his turban will be like the clouds, his armor the full mail of the Messenger of Allah, and his sword the sword of the Messenger of Allah, Dhu al-Faqar. He will draw the sword on his shoulder for eight months, killing in a frenzy. First, he will begin with Bani Shayba, cutting off their hands and hanging them on the Kaaba, and his caller will cry out: 'These are the thieves of Allah.' Then he will turn to Quraysh, taking nothing from them except the sword, and giving them nothing except the sword.'
And the Qa'im will not appear until two books are read: one in Basra, and one in Kufa, declaring the acquittance/dismissal of Ali (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What are the signs and attributes of the Qa'im according to Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological transition marked by the 'completion of the chain' (tammilat al-halqa), interpreted by Shia scholars as the gathering of ten thousand elite supporters. It emphasizes the continuity of prophetic authority through the physical relics of the Prophet—specifically the banner of Paradise and the armor of the Battle of Uhud—passed down to Imam Ali and preserved until the Qa'im's emergence. The text underscores the purging of political rivals, particularly Bani Shayba and Quraysh, and the prerequisite reading of two books of allegiance to Ali, linking the Mahdi's rise to the consolidation of divine justice.
